title: The Chemist Who Was Owed a Country: Motol to the Garden at Rehovot

segments.name: The Pale, and the Chemistry of Dyes

stops.name: Motol, birth on the Pina
stops.date_confidence: attested. Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'. Two corrections carried from the verification pass: the governorate and the pin. Motol sat in the Kobrinsky Uyezd of Grodno Governorate until 1917 (Wikipedia, 'Motal'), not Minsk Governorate, which held Pinsk. The pool's pin 52.1667, 25.95 fell about 26 km east in open country; Wikipedia, 'Motal' gives 52 deg 08 min N, 25 deg 36 min E, used here. No house or landmark survives in the village to fix a tighter point.
stops.campa: Chaim Azriel Weizmann is born in a timber merchant's house in Motol, a village of the Pale on the Pina, third of fifteen children of Oizer Weizmann and Rachel Leah Czemerinsky. The family floats logs down toward the Baltic. The boy learns Hebrew in the heder before he learns Russian anywhere, and the village he learns it in belongs to the Kobrinsky district of Grodno Governorate, not to Minsk, whatever the later biographies say. Pinsk, twenty-five miles east, will do duty as his address for the rest of his life. Nothing in Motol marks the house.
suggested_refs: The village of Motal, Ivanava District, Brest Region, Belarus, on the Pina

stops.name: Pinsk, the Real-Gymnasium
stops.date_confidence: attested for the fact, approximate for the date. Wikipedia gives heder from early childhood, entry to the Pinsk Real-Gymnasium at about eleven, and graduation with honours in 1892; no enrolment date is recorded, so the year is computed from his age and the month and day default to 01. The school building's own coordinates are not in any source consulted, and the stop sits at the Pinsk city pin.
stops.campa: At about eleven he is sent east to Pinsk and the Russian secondary school, the first of his family into a gentile classroom. He is good at chemistry and knows it. In a town where Hovevei Zion circles meet in back rooms he picks up a second education alongside the first, and nobody sets him an examination in that one. He graduates with distinction in 1892. The numerus clausus is in force across the Russian universities, and none of them will take him.
suggested_refs: The Russian Real-Gymnasium at Pinsk, exact building unidentified in the reachable sources

stops.name: Darmstadt, the Technische Hochschule
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day unknown and defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Barred from the Russian universities by the numerus clausus, he goes to Germany at seventeen and enrols at the Technische Hochschule in Darmstadt to read chemistry. He keeps himself by teaching Hebrew at a local Jewish school, travelling out to the lessons, poor in a way he will describe without embarrassment for the rest of his life. German laboratory practice in the 1890s is the best in the world, and dye chemistry is its commercial heart: the science the great firms pay for, and the one an outsider can sell. The fees come out of the Hebrew lessons.
suggested_refs: The Technische Hochschule Darmstadt, chemistry faculty of the early 1890s

stops.name: Berlin-Charlottenburg, dyes and the student circles
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day unknown and defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He transfers to the Technische Hochschule at Charlottenburg and settles into aromatic chemistry and synthetic dyes, the most commercial science in Europe. Berlin also holds the Russian-Jewish student circles, and there he falls in with Leo Motzkin and Nahum Sokolow, arguing Zionism in Russian in German lodging houses. Neither occupation is a hobby and neither is a cover for the other; he will still be running both at seventy. Which of them he took more seriously at twenty is not a question his student years answer.
suggested_refs: The Russian-Jewish Academic Society of Berlin, meeting-place of Motzkin's circle

stops.name: Fribourg, the doctorate and the promise
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the doctorate (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day defaulted. The move to Fribourg is 1897. The engagement to Sophia Getzowa is carried in the pool at both 1897 and 1898 and the divergence is left standing here: Wikipedia places the Fribourg move in 1897 and then says 'That year he became engaged to Sophia Getzowa', and the relationship is said to have run four years before he told her of Vera Khatzman in 1900, which fits 1897. The campa asserts no year for it.
stops.campa: In these Swiss years he becomes engaged to Sophia Getzowa, a medical student, a promise that will hold four years and then break. Switzerland in the late 1890s is where Russian Jews barred from study at home come to study, and the lodging houses of Fribourg, Bern and Geneva are full of them, a doctorate in one hand and the Basel Program in the other. He moves to Fribourg in 1897 for doctoral work and the university confers the degree in 1899. The subject is organic chemistry, which is what he will still be working on fifty years later at Rehovot.
suggested_refs: The University of Fribourg doctoral thesis in organic chemistry, 1899

stops.name: Geneva, Vera Khatzman
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day defaulted. Pin corrected from the pool's 46.1955, 6.1447, which fell about 410 m south: Wikipedia, 'University of Geneva' gives 46 deg 11 min 57 sec N, 6 deg 8 min 42 sec E for Uni Bastions. The mock-trial detail in the campa is [R], resting on biographical tradition (Norman Rose and related accounts) and not independently verified.
stops.campa: He joins the organic chemistry department at Geneva, is made assistant lecturer, and here meets Vera Khatzman, a Russian medical student eleven years younger. The engagement to Sophia Getzowa has run four years by the time he says anything; student tradition holds that his own circle staged a mock trial over it and told him to keep his word. He does not keep it. Vera Khatzman qualifies in medicine, follows him to England, and practises there in infant welfare while he does chemistry and politics.
suggested_refs: The Uni Bastions building of the University of Geneva, organic chemistry department

segments.name: Basel: the Fraction Against the Diplomat

stops.name: Basel, the Second Congress
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool gives the year only, and the exact date is inherited byte-identical from theodor_herzl.journey.json, which places the Second Congress at 28 August 1898. The coordinate is likewise inherited from theodor_herzl.journey.json, martin_buber.journey.json and samuel_preiswerk.journey.json. Two other pins for the same hall are in circulation and are recorded rather than followed: 47.5596, 7.5886 in ahad_ha_am.journey.json, and 47.5556, 7.5878 in this subject's own research pool. de.wikipedia gives 47.554444, 7.589444 for the Stadtcasino.
stops.campa: He misses the First Congress the year before, unable to make the journey. At the Second, in the Musiksaal of the Stadtcasino on the Steinenberg, he takes his place among the delegates of Theodor Herzl's parliament without a country, and begins an attendance that will run, with two long interruptions, for very nearly half a century. He is twenty-three, a doctoral student in dyes, one voice among several hundred. Herzl is at the rostrum in evening dress, staging a state that does not exist.
suggested_refs: The Musiksaal of the Stadtcasino Basel, seat of the Zionist Congresses

stops.name: Basel, the Democratic Fraction
stops.date_confidence: attested. Date inherited byte-identical from ahad_ha_am.journey.json and theodor_herzl.journey.json, both of which put the Fifth Congress at 26 December 1901. Coordinate inherited from the theodor_herzl / martin_buber / samuel_preiswerk pin rather than from ahad_ha_am's 47.5596, 7.5886; the divergence is about 450 m and is recorded, not resolved.
stops.campa: At the Fifth Congress four young men organize the Democratic Fraction against Herzl's method of pure diplomacy: Weizmann, Martin Buber, Leo Motzkin and Berthold Feiwel, claiming Ahad Ha'am as their cultural authority without his participation. Everything later called Synthetic Zionism is visible here already, and it is visible in opposition. What they want is culture, schools, settlement on the ground and a Jewish university in Palestine, and they want it before any charter arrives from a sultan.
suggested_refs: The memorandum for a Jewish university circulated by Weizmann, Buber and Feiwel from 1901

stops.name: Berlin, the Judischer Verlag
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (martin_buber.journey.json, recording the 1902 founding); month and day unknown and defaulted to 01. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from martin_buber.journey.json. Weizmann is a founder, so the stop is his own and not borrowed.
stops.campa: With Buber, Berthold Feiwel and the illustrator E. M. Lilien he helps found the Judischer Verlag, a publishing house for a national Jewish culture that as yet has no nation to sit in. Books, prints, an almanac. A press is a cheap way to make a people visible to itself, and it can be run from a city where almost none of its readers live. He is one of its founders and none of its writers; his own trade is still aromatic chemistry, done at a bench. The first titles come out of Berlin in 1902.
suggested_refs: The Judischer Verlag, Berlin, founded 1902

segments.name: Manchester: Aniline, Liberals, and a Marsh

stops.name: Manchester, the chemistry department
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day defaulted. The Clayton Aniline consultancy is dated 1905 and the naturalization 1910, both folded into this stop because the pool attaches no place to either beyond the city and the country; neither is given a pin of its own.
stops.campa: He arrives in England at twenty-nine with poor English and no position, and is taken on in the chemistry department at Manchester, rising to senior lecturer. Within a year he is consulting for the Clayton Aniline Company, and the industrial work pays better than the university does. Manchester is also a Liberal city with a Guardian, and he begins the slow business of knowing people: C. P. Scott the editor, manufacturers, members of parliament. The introductions turn out to be worth more to him than the laboratory. In 1910 he takes British nationality, on papers said to have been signed by the Home Secretary, Winston Churchill.
suggested_refs: The Clayton Aniline Company dye works, Manchester
The Manchester Guardian under C. P. Scott

stops.name: Zoppot, the marriage
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01. Place corrected from the pool, which had the marriage in Switzerland: Wikipedia, 'Vera Weizmann' states that in 1906 she married him in Zoppot, West Prussia, present-day Sopot, Poland.
stops.campa: He marries Vera Khatzman at Zoppot on the Baltic, in West Prussia, a spa town reachable from both their families and belonging to neither of their futures. She is newly qualified in medicine; he is thirty-one, a lecturer in an English industrial city she has not yet seen. They will live in Manchester, then in London through a war, then in a white house at Rehovot built for them by an architect driven out of Germany. Two sons, Benjamin in 1907 and Michael in 1916.
suggested_refs: Zoppot, West Prussia, now Sopot, Poland

stops.name: Manchester, Balfour and the marsh
stops.date_confidence: the meeting is attested; the year is disputed between 1905 and 1906 in the pool's own sources, and the dialogue is [R]. Coordinate and date both inherited byte-identical from arthur_balfour.journey.json, which carries the stop at 1906 and names Charles Dreyfus as the intermediary. The exact meeting site within Manchester is unconfirmed. The pool's first draft of the exchange, an analogy about abandoning Jerusalem as an Englishman would abandon London, was garbled and is not used; the Saskatchewan and marsh version follows Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann', which itself follows Trial and Error (1949).
stops.campa: Charles Dreyfus brings the chemist to the member for East Manchester during a campaign, and Balfour asks why the Zionists will not take the offer of a territory in East Africa. Weizmann answers with a question: would Balfour give up London to live in Saskatchewan? Balfour says the British have always had London. Weizmann says that his people lived in Jerusalem when London was still a marsh. The exchange survives in one place only, Weizmann's own memoir, written forty years afterward by a man with every reason to make it shapely.
stops.quote: Yes, and we lived in Jerusalem when London was still a marsh.
stops.quote_source: Weizmann to Arthur Balfour, Manchester, 1905 or 1906, as recorded in his autobiography Trial and Error (1949); memoir, not transcript
suggested_refs: Trial and Error (1949), the Manchester chapters
arthur_balfour.journey.json, stop 'Manchester, the chemist and the Uganda offer'

stops.name: Jerusalem, the first sight of the country
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day unknown and defaulted to 01. The Old City pin stands for a visit that covered more of Ottoman Palestine than Jerusalem alone.
stops.campa: He goes for the first time to Ottoman Palestine at thirty-two, having argued about it for ten years without seeing it. What he finds confirms the commitment and disgusts him with the method: philanthropic colonies on subsidy, administrators, dependence, no industry, no science, no economy that could stand alone. He comes back to Manchester arguing for practical work done by Jews on the ground rather than paid for out of Paris. He is in the country some weeks, and does not return to it for eleven years.
suggested_refs: The Rothschild-subsidized colonies of Ottoman Palestine, inspected 1907

stops.name: London, Carlton Gardens
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from arthur_balfour.journey.json, stop 'Carlton Gardens'.
stops.campa: Four months into the war he comes to Balfour's house at Carlton Gardens, and finds the door open in a way it was not in Manchester. Balfour tells him the Zionist project is a great cause and that he understands it. There is no policy behind the sentence and no promise inside it, and Weizmann leaves with nothing he could show to anybody. What he has instead is a Foreign Secretary in waiting who will take his telephone calls. He is at that moment still a lecturer in chemistry at Manchester.
stops.quote: It is a great cause and I understand it.
stops.quote_source: Arthur Balfour to Weizmann at Carlton Gardens, 12 December 1914, as carried in arthur_balfour.journey.json
suggested_refs: Balfour's house at 4 Carlton Gardens, London

stops.name: Bromley-by-Bow, thirty thousand tons of acetone
stops.date_confidence: the fermentation work is attested to 1915 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day defaulted. Site corrected: the pool pinned a 'J. and W. Nicholson distillery, Bow' at 51.5292, -0.0246, about 1.5 km west of the works. Wikipedia, 'J and W Nicholson and Co' records that the firm bought the Three Mills Distillery at Bromley-by-Bow on the River Lea in 1872 and that Three Mills was used by the government to produce acetone in the first world war. The attribution of the pilot work to Nicholson's remains a synthesis of scientific-biography accounts, not a primary document.
stops.campa: The Royal Navy is short of cordite, cordite needs acetone, and the blockade has cut the supply. Weizmann has an anaerobic bacterium that turns starch into acetone, butanol and ethanol, and he has made it in cubic centimetres on a bench. He is asked for thirty thousand tons. The pilot plant goes into the Three Mills distillery at Bromley-by-Bow on the Lea, the old Nicholson gin works, and the process is scaled from a laboratory to a nation's war supply. The bacterium is fed on maize until the maize runs short, and then on horse chestnuts.
stops.quote: Well, Dr. Weizmann, we need thirty thousand tons of acetone. Can you make it?
stops.quote_source: Winston Churchill to Weizmann, as recorded by Weizmann in Trial and Error (1949), quoted in Winston Churchill: Finest Hour, issue 170, 'Churchill and Chaim Weizmann'
suggested_refs: The Three Mills Distillery, Bromley-by-Bow, on the River Lea
Clostridium acetobutylicum and the ABE fermentation
sources: Wikipedia, 'J and W Nicholson and Co'

stops.name: Holland Park, the house on Addison Road
stops.date_confidence: the London residence is attested to the war years; no year is fixed in the pool and 1916 is chosen to sit the stop mid-war, with month and day defaulted. The house number is contested and is not resolved here: Wikipedia gives 16 Addison Road, while English Heritage's blue plaque to Weizmann, erected 1980, is at 67 Addison Road, W14 8JL, approximately 51.4999, -0.2072. The plaque address and coordinate are used because English Heritage researches plaque addresses from residence records, and the conflict is recorded rather than adjudicated.
stops.campa: He keeps a house on Addison Road in Holland Park and works out of it in three directions at once: fermentation for the Ministry of Munitions, a chemistry post he still holds in Manchester, and a Zionist diplomacy conducted in drawing rooms with men who do not always know they are negotiating. Vera Weizmann keeps the house and her own practice. Trains north and cabs to Whitehall are what the making of the Balfour Declaration actually consists of, and nothing in it is filed as a campaign. Two numbers on that road are recorded for him, 16 and 67; the plaque went up on 67.
suggested_refs: The English Heritage blue plaque to Weizmann at 67 Addison Road, London W14
sources: English Heritage blue plaque register, Addison Road

stops.name: London, the drafts read to Ahad Ha'am
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from ahad_ha_am.journey.json, which dates the London consultation to June 1917 with the day defaulted.
stops.campa: Ahad Ha'am is in London, old, holding no office, commanding no following, and Weizmann brings him the drafts. The argument is over a formula: a national home, not a Jewish nationality, because the second would hand every European government a reason to ask its own Jews where they really belonged. Ahad Ha'am's name goes onto no draft and into no cabinet minute, and his reading is in the wording that survives. Sixteen years earlier at Basel, Weizmann had claimed him as the Fraction's authority without asking him first. He asks him now, in a room, about wording.
suggested_refs: ahad_ha_am.journey.json, the June 1917 London stop on the Declaration drafts

stops.name: London, King Charles Street
stops.date_confidence: attested for the August revision; day defaulted to 01. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from arthur_balfour.journey.json, whose Foreign Office drafting stop is filed under a 1916 date but covers the 1917 drafting.
stops.campa: Through the summer the drafts move between the Zionist office and the Foreign Office: Weizmann and Sokolow write, Balfour revises in August, the War Cabinet argues. Edwin Montagu, the only Jew in the cabinet, fights the whole thing as an invitation to tell British Jews they are foreigners. Weizmann has spent thirteen years making himself the man these rooms telephone, and the room where the text is settled is one he waits outside. The Foreign Office wants Russian and American Jewish opinion held to the Allied side, and says so in its own minutes.
suggested_refs: The Foreign Office, King Charles Street, and the successive Zionist drafts of 1917

stops.name: London, the second of November
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from arthur_balfour.journey.json, stop 'the second of November', corroborated on the same date in ahad_ha_am.journey.json. New Court on St Swithin's Lane as the physical receiving point of the letter is [R], an inference from the addressee and not verified against a primary document, and it is therefore named in the campa and refs rather than given a pin.
stops.campa: The War Cabinet approves the text on the thirty-first of October. On the second of November Balfour signs the covering letter to Lord Rothschild: sixty-seven words viewing with favour the establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people. Weizmann has negotiated toward it for three years and argued its drafts line by line. He is not the addressee and his name is not on the paper, which carries Balfour's. It goes to the Zionist Federation by way of the Rothschild bank at New Court, on St Swithin's Lane in the City.
suggested_refs: New Court, N M Rothschild and Sons, St Swithin's Lane, London

segments.name: The Commission, the Emir, and the Peace

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Zionist Commission
stops.date_confidence: attested to April 1918 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); day defaulted to 01. The commission's headquarters coordinate is the pool's approximation to central Jerusalem, not a fixed address.
stops.campa: He lands in a country still half inside the war, at the head of a commission the British government has authorized to speak for Jewish interests to the military administration. Allenby's officers regard the Declaration as an embarrassment they have been handed to administer. Weizmann tours the colonies, inspects, argues about water and land registry, and finds that the Arab population of Palestine was consulted about none of it. In July he lays the foundation stones of the Hebrew University on Mount Scopus, with guns still audible to the north.
suggested_refs: The Zionist Commission of 1918 and its dealings with the British military administration

stops.name: Near Aqaba, the camp of Emir Faisal
stops.date_confidence: the meeting is attested to June 1918 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); the day, the camp's coordinates and the T. E. Lawrence brokerage all come from the pool's synthesis of standard accounts rather than from a source fetched in the verification pass, and are [R].
stops.campa: He rides out to Emir Faisal ibn Hussein in the desert east of Aqaba, brought by British officers who have decided the two men should talk. Faisal is running the Arab Revolt. Weizmann is running a commission with sixty-seven words behind it. They speak through interpreters about a Jewish Palestine and an Arab kingdom, both of them resting on a British empire that has promised each of them something it has also promised the other. They meet for an hour or two and part on good terms.
suggested_refs: The Faisal encampment near Aqaba, June 1918, meeting brokered through British officers

stops.name: London, the Carlton Hotel
stops.date_confidence: attested. Venue corrected from the pool, which placed the signing in Paris and fell back on a generic Charing Cross pin: Wikipedia, 'Faisal-Weizmann Agreement' gives the Carlton Hotel, London, Haymarket at Pall Mall, on 3 January 1919. The memorandum named in Faisal's reservation is dated 4 January 1919, the day after the signing.
stops.campa: At the Carlton Hotel on the Haymarket, Weizmann and Faisal sign nine articles: an Arab state and a Jewish Palestine as separate polities in cooperation, large-scale Jewish immigration, British arbitration of disputes, the Muslim holy places left under Muslim control. The agreement is signed and published. At the foot of the sheet, in his own hand and in Arabic, Faisal writes a reservation voiding the whole of it if the Arabs do not get the independence he has demanded in a memorandum dated the following day. They do not get it.
stops.quote: Provided the Arabs obtain their independence as demanded in my Memorandum dated the 4th of January 1919... but if the slightest modification or departure were to be made I shall not then be bound by a single word of the present agreement which shall be deemed void.
stops.quote_source: Emir Faisal's handwritten Arabic reservation on the Faisal-Weizmann Agreement, London, 3 January 1919, as given in Wikipedia, 'Faisal-Weizmann Agreement'
suggested_refs: The Carlton Hotel, Haymarket, demolished 1957
The nine articles of the Faisal-Weizmann Agreement

stops.name: Paris, the Quai d'Orsay
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1919 for the statement of Zionist aims; day defaulted to 01. The pool's broader window for his Peace Conference work is January to June 1919. The quotation's citation is corrected from the pool's vague 'public statements on Zionist aims' to the Paris Peace Conference occasion and its two real references.
stops.campa: He appears at the Peace Conference to ask not for a state but for a mandate and a chance: conditions under which Jews could come and build until the country was theirs by the weight of what they had made. He is careful about the wording. Balfour will not be careful; that August, in a memorandum to Curzon, he writes that Britain does not propose to consult the wishes of the present inhabitants and that Zionism outweighs the desires of seven hundred thousand Arabs. The Council of Ten hears Weizmann for one afternoon.
stops.quote: establish such a society in Palestine that Palestine shall be as Jewish as England is English, or America American.
stops.quote_source: Statement of Zionist aims at the Paris Peace Conference, February 1919; cited in William L. Cleveland, A History of the Modern Middle East (Westview, 2004), p. 228, and Weizmann, Trial and Error
suggested_refs: Balfour's memorandum 132187/2117/44A to Curzon, 11 August 1919

stops.name: London, Keren Hayesod
stops.date_confidence: attested; the London congress ran 7 to 24 July 1920. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from ze_ev_jabotinsky.journey.json.
stops.campa: The World Zionist Congress meets in London and founds Keren Hayesod, the fund that will actually buy the land and pay for the settling of it, with Weizmann, Albert Einstein and Vladimir Jabotinsky among its early names. The movement now has a treasury and an executive, and what it has not got is any agreement inside itself about how fast to go. Weizmann becomes president of the World Zionist Organization the same year and holds the office for eleven. The following year he brings Jabotinsky onto the Executive to run information work.
suggested_refs: Keren Hayesod, founded at the London Zionist Congress, July 1920

stops.name: New York, the Hotel Commodore
stops.date_confidence: attested to the evening of 2 April 1921 (Smithsonian Magazine, 'One Hundred Years Ago, Einstein Was Given a Hero's Welcome by America's Jews'). The coordinate is this file's own approximation to the hotel's East Forty-second Street site; no pin for the Commodore exists in the pool, whose alternatives were a generic New York point and the Biltmore. The pool had also attached the quoted phrase to the wrong occasion, giving it as the arrival in Manhattan; per the article it describes the end of the Lower East Side motorcade, reaching the hotel at 11:30 p.m.
stops.campa: He crosses to America with Albert Einstein to raise the endowment for the Hebrew University. Tugs come out into the harbour with bands. The motorcade, instead of driving to the hotel, is taken slowly through the Jewish streets of the Lower East Side, where the crowds have come for the physicist. Weizmann is president of the Zionist Organization and the man with the plan for the money; in New York it is Einstein the streets want. They reach the Hotel Commodore on Forty-second Street at half past eleven at night, tired, hungry, thirsty and completely dazed.
stops.quote: tired, hungry, thirsty and completely dazed
stops.quote_source: Weizmann's recollection of the end of the Lower East Side motorcade with Einstein, reaching the Hotel Commodore at 11:30 p.m., 2 April 1921, quoted in Smithsonian Magazine, 'One Hundred Years Ago, Einstein Was Given a Hero's Welcome by America's Jews'
suggested_refs: The Hotel Commodore, East 42nd Street, New York

stops.name: Cleveland, the break with Brandeis
stops.date_confidence: [R] and imprecise. The pool gives the year 1921 and no month, so the date defaults to 1921-01-01, which places this stop earlier in the calendar than the April tour it actually followed; the segment keeps the historical order rather than the date order and says so here. The convention and its outcome are the pool's synthesis of standard Zionist-movement historiography, with no primary account of the proceedings refetched.
stops.campa: The American Zionists led by Louis Brandeis want the movement run like a well-audited investment: no central political organization, money raised in America and spent under American accounting, Palestine as a development project with a balance sheet. Weizmann wants a movement with a centre, and the centre is where he is. At the convention in Cleveland the two positions are put to a vote and Weizmann's side wins. Brandeis and his people resign the leadership of the Zionist Organization of America and take their accounting with them. The year is 1921; the month is not recorded.
suggested_refs: The 1921 Cleveland convention of the Zionist Organization of America

stops.name: London, Jabotinsky resigns
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from ze_ev_jabotinsky.journey.json.
stops.campa: Two years after Weizmann brought him onto the Executive to run information work, Vladimir Jabotinsky resigns from it, and shortly afterward from the Zionist Organization altogether, over pace and over words. He wants the word state said out loud and he wants Jewish battalions. He calls the alternative Weizmann's method, meaning patience, good relations with British power, and the assumption that the mandatory can be talked round. The two men are never reconciled.
suggested_refs: ze_ev_jabotinsky.journey.json, the January 1923 resignation stop

stops.name: Mount Scopus, the university opens
stops.date_confidence: attested. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from arthur_balfour.journey.json, corroborated in ahad_ha_am.journey.json and einstein.journey.json. Two divergent pins for the same hill are recorded and not resolved: 31.7788, 35.2396 in einstein.journey.json for a 1923 lecture there, and 31.7936, 35.2447 flagged in martin_buber.journey.json. Honest gap: the cited source lists Balfour, Allenby, Churchill and Herbert Samuel as present but does not explicitly place Weizmann on the platform that day, and the campa does not claim he was.
stops.campa: The Hebrew University opens on the ridge north of Jerusalem, twenty-three years after Weizmann, Buber and Feiwel circulated a memorandum arguing for it and seven years after the foundation stones went down. Balfour comes out at Weizmann's invitation to open it, an old man reading an address in a hot amphitheatre, with Allenby and Herbert Samuel on the platform beside him. The endowment was raised four years before in American halls where the crowds had come to see Einstein. Whether Weizmann himself stood on that platform, the sources naming the guests do not say.
suggested_refs: The 1918 cornerstone-laying on Mount Scopus

stops.name: Hook Heath, the last visit to Balfour
stops.date_confidence: attested that the visit took place shortly before Balfour's death. Coordinate and date inherited byte-identical from arthur_balfour.journey.json, where the stop is filed under the death date of 19 March 1930; the visit itself was some days earlier and this file does not narrow it.
stops.campa: He goes down to Woking, to Balfour's brother's house at Hook Heath, to sit with the dying man. Twenty-four years earlier he had told him, in a room borrowed for an election campaign, that Jews lived in Jerusalem when London was a marsh; he had been a lecturer nobody in politics had heard of, and Balfour had been amused enough to remember it. What passed between them at the end is not recorded by either man in any form that survives. Balfour dies on the nineteenth of March.

stops.name: Basel, the presidency lost
stops.date_confidence: the loss of the presidency at the 1931 Zionist Congress is attested (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'; Jewish Virtual Library). The pool names neither the month nor the city, so both are this file's inference: month and day default to 01, and the stop is placed at the standing Basel congress pin on the ground that the 17th Congress sat there, which is [R] and not from the pool.
stops.campa: The Passfield White Paper of 1930 proposes limits on land purchase and on immigration, and thirty years of Weizmann's method, which is trust in British good faith, are on the table with it. He resigns in protest. MacDonald writes a letter softening the paper. The Congress votes him out anyway, having worked out that the man who is friends with the British is the wrong man to have on the day the British stop being friends. He has held the presidency eleven years and will hold it again from 1935.
suggested_refs: The Passfield White Paper, October 1930, and the MacDonald letter of February 1931

segments.name: Rehovot, and the Closing of the Doors

stops.name: Rehovot, the Daniel Sieff Research Institute
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1934 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); month and day defaulted. The campus pin is distinct from the Weizmann House pin used elsewhere in this file: the house is at 31.9065, 34.8186, about a kilometre east.
stops.campa: Out of office, he does what he did at twenty and builds a laboratory. Israel and Rebecca Sieff and the Marks family pay for a research institute at Rehovot in memory of their son Daniel; Weizmann had hoped Fritz Haber would direct it and lost him to death within the year, so he directs it himself. He goes back to organic chemistry and fuel research at sixty, in a country he has spent his life arguing about and has hardly ever lived in. In 1901 the Fraction had argued that a people is built by schools and science before it is built by charters. The institute opens in 1934 and he is its director.
stops.quote: I trust and feel sure in my heart that science will bring to this land both peace and a renewal of its youth, creating here the springs of a new spiritual and material life. [...] I speak of both science for its own sake and science as a means to an end.
stops.quote_source: Weizmann on the founding of the Daniel Sieff Research Institute, 1934, cited in Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann' from Weizmann Institute historical materials
suggested_refs: The Daniel Sieff Research Institute, Rehovot, opened 1934, renamed for Weizmann in 1949

stops.name: Jerusalem, before the Peel Commission
stops.date_confidence: the testimony and its date are attested (The Letters and Papers of Chaim Weizmann: Series B, Transaction, 1983, p. 102). The place is not: the pool gives no location for it. The stop is placed at the Jerusalem pin on the ground that the Commission's public hearings of late 1936 sat in Palestine, and that inference is this file's and is [R].
stops.campa: He gives evidence to the royal commission under Lord Peel in the year of the Arab general strike, and puts the case not as a claim of right but as an arithmetic of doors: six million people in central and eastern Europe for whom the world is divided into places where they cannot live and places where they cannot enter. The commission will recommend partition, the first official proposal to cut the country in two. Weizmann accepts partition. Much of the movement does not, and says so loudly enough to be heard in London.
stops.quote: for whom the world is divided into places where they cannot live and places where they cannot enter
stops.quote_source: Testimony to the Peel Commission, 25 November 1936, in The Letters and Papers of Chaim Weizmann: Series B (Transaction Publishers, 1983), p. 102
suggested_refs: The report of the Palestine Royal Commission (Peel), July 1937

stops.name: St James's Palace, the White Paper
stops.date_confidence: attested to 1939 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); the pool gives no month for the conference and both month and day default to 01. The conference in fact sat in February and March 1939 and the White Paper followed in May, and this file does not assert those months because the pool does not carry them.
stops.campa: The British convene Jews and Arabs in the same palace and, because the Arab delegations will not sit down with the Jewish ones, hold two conferences in two rooms with the same ministers walking between them. Weizmann argues for the mandate as he has read it for twenty-two years. The White Paper that follows caps Jewish immigration at seventy-five thousand over five years and then makes it conditional on Arab consent, in the spring of 1939, with Germany in Prague and the doors of Europe closing one at a time. He calls it a breach of faith. It remains British policy through the whole of the war.
suggested_refs: The 1939 White Paper on Palestine
The St James's Conference, February to March 1939

stops.name: London, the letter to Chamberlain
stops.date_confidence: the letter's date is given as 29 August 1939 and is consistent with the report of it, but the verification pass did not open the archive page itself, so the date is cited via the Jewish Telegraphic Agency's report of 6 September 1939 rather than as independently verified. The London pin is the standing one, used because the pool attaches no address.
stops.campa: Four months after the White Paper and three days before Germany invades Poland, he writes to the Prime Minister putting the Jewish Agency's men and its resources at Britain's disposal. The policy he has fought all year stands and will stand through the war; he offers anyway. The Agency will raise brigades for an army whose government is at that moment turning refugee ships away from the coast of Palestine. Chamberlain's office lets it be known that the offer will be kept in mind. Weizmann is sixty-four.
stops.quote: I wish to confirm in the most explicit manner the declarations which I and my colleagues have made during the last month and especially in the last week: that the Jews stand by Great Britain and will fight on the side of the democracies.
stops.quote_source: Weizmann's letter to Neville Chamberlain, 29 August 1939, reported in the Jewish Telegraphic Agency, 6 September 1939
suggested_refs: Jewish Telegraphic Agency, 'Chamberlain Welcomes Agency's War Aid; Says It Will Be Kept in Mind', 6 September 1939

stops.name: Rehovot, the news from the Bay of Biscay
stops.date_confidence: attested to February 1942 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'; Times of Israel, 27 November 2024, giving his age as 25 and the body as never recovered); day defaulted to 01. Coordinate corrected from the pool's 31.9061, 34.8074, which fell about a kilometre west on the institute campus: Wikipedia, 'Weizmann House' gives 31 deg 54 min 23.23 sec N, 34 deg 49 min 6.83 sec E. The Commonwealth War Graves Commission listing was not fetched and is not claimed here.
stops.campa: The house at Rehovot was built for them in the mid-1930s by Erich Mendelsohn, a modernist driven out of Germany: white, low, a round staircase tower, citrus around it. In February 1942 word comes that Flight Lieutenant Michael Oser Weizmann, of No. 502 Squadron, is missing after an operational flight over the Bay of Biscay. He is twenty-five. The aircraft is not found and the body is never recovered. His father goes on writing testamentary provision for a son who might still come back.

stops.name: New York, the Biltmore Conference
stops.date_confidence: attested to May 1942 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); day defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: Six hundred delegates in a Manhattan hotel adopt the program that ends forty years of careful wording: a Jewish Commonwealth in Palestine, unrestricted immigration, the Jewish Agency in control of it. The conference sits three months after his son's aircraft went into the Bay of Biscay, and Weizmann accepts the turn to open statehood. What is happening in Europe is known in outline by then and not yet in full. David Ben-Gurion authors the program. He is by now the actual centre of the movement, and everyone in the ballroom can see it.
suggested_refs: The Biltmore Program, adopted at the Hotel Biltmore, New York, May 1942

segments.name: A State, and a Ceremonial Office

stops.name: Basel, the last congress
stops.date_confidence: attested; the non-reelection is dated to December 1946 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann') and the presidential statement quoted here to 9 December 1946, which fixes the day. Coordinate inherited from the standing Basel congress pin used in theodor_herzl.journey.json, martin_buber.journey.json and samuel_preiswerk.journey.json.
stops.campa: He comes to the twenty-second Congress at seventy-two, nearly blind, to defend the British orientation of a lifetime before a movement that has watched the White Paper hold through the extermination of European Jewry and has stopped listening to him. He speaks against the armed underground and against the cult of heroic destruction: Massada, for all its heroism, was a disaster in our history. The Congress does not reelect him, and he leaves holding no office in the organization he led for nineteen years. He has been coming to Basel congresses since 1898.
stops.quote: Massada, for all its heroism, was a disaster in our history; It is not our purpose or our right to plunge to destruction in order to bequeath a legend of martyrdom to posterity; Zionism was to mark the end of our glorious deaths and the beginning of a new path leading to life.
stops.quote_source: Presidential statement to the Zionist Congress, Basel, 9 December 1946, in The Letters and Papers of Chaim Weizmann, Series B, Papers vol. II (Yad Chaim Weizmann, 1984), Paper 87, pp. 636-37

stops.name: Jerusalem, before the committee
stops.date_confidence: attested that Weizmann testified before UNSCOP as a private citizen during its twelve public hearings of 4 to 17 July 1947 (Wikipedia, 'United Nations Special Committee on Palestine'); the exact day of his appearance is not fixed in the pool and defaults to 01. This stop replaces the pool's erroneous Flushing Meadows placement, which put his 1947 testimony before the General Assembly plenary in New York. The Jerusalem coordinate is an approximation to the hearing city, not to a hall.
stops.campa: The United Nations Special Committee on Palestine holds twelve public hearings between the fourth and the seventeenth of July, and Weizmann appears before it as a private citizen, holding no position in any Jewish body. He is the most famous Zionist alive and he testifies as nobody's representative. What he has instead of office is thirty years of being the man the British and the Americans already knew, and a voice that still carries in rooms where votes get counted. He speaks for the partition of the country.

stops.name: Lake Success, the argument for the Negev
stops.date_confidence: attested to October 1947 for the address on the Negev to the Ad Hoc Committee at Lake Success; day defaulted to 01. The coordinate is an approximation to Lake Success, New York, supplied by the verification pass rather than by a fetched source, and is not a pin on the hall.
stops.campa: At Lake Success he argues before the Ad Hoc Committee that the Negev belongs inside the Jewish state: empty desert, worth nothing on a surveyor's report, half the territory in question, and the only room left to put people in. The argument is chemical as much as political, because he has been looking at that desert since the Zionist Commission of 1918 and knows what is dissolved in it. Nobody in the room has to be told who he is. The Negev is in the partition plan the General Assembly votes on in November.

stops.name: The White House, the eighteenth of March
stops.date_confidence: attested to 18 March 1948 and broadly documented across Truman-era scholarship; the pool notes that no primary transcript was refetched in the verification pass, so the content of the exchange is [R] and the meeting itself [A].
stops.campa: Truman has stopped seeing Zionists. Eddie Jacobson, who sold shirts with him in Kansas City, walks into the Oval Office and asks him to see one old man; Truman agrees on the condition that nobody is told about it. Weizmann is brought in through the east gate. He asks for statehood and for the Negev, and Truman tells him recognition will follow a declaration properly made. The State Department, which does not know the meeting happened, spends the following day arguing publicly for a United Nations trusteeship instead.

stops.name: Tel Aviv, elected in absentia
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date. City corrected from the pool, which placed the Provisional State Council in Jerusalem at 31.7807, 35.2192: Wikipedia, 'Provisional State Council' records that the council met in Tel Aviv at the Jewish National Fund building, where Moetzet HaAm had convened on 14 May to vote the Declaration, and Jerusalem was under siege in May 1948. The Rothschild Boulevard coordinate is an approximation to that quarter. Weizmann was in the United States and not present.
stops.campa: Two days after the declaration is read aloud in the hall on Rothschild Boulevard, the Provisional State Council elects Weizmann its president. He is in the United States and learns of it there. The office is a title with a residence attached: Ben-Gurion holds the government, the army and the war, and has held them in fact for a decade. Weizmann has argued for forty-eight years that a state is made by a people building it and not by anybody's decree. He is four thousand miles from the hall, raising money.
stops.quote: A state cannot be created by decree, but by the forces of a people and in the course of generations. Even if all the governments of the world gave us a country, it would only be a gift of words. But if the Jewish people will go build Palestine, the Jewish State will become a reality—a fact.
stops.quote_source: The Letters and Papers of Chaim Weizmann, Papers vol. I: August 1898 - July 1931 (Transaction Publishers, 1983), p. 301

The Provisional State Council, 16 May 1948 to 17 February 1949

stops.name: The White House, the Torah scroll
stops.date_confidence: [R]. The pool carries this as a synthesis of standard Truman-recognition historiography and not from a primary account refetched in the verification pass. The date and the scroll are the pool's; the qualification about Clifford and the American Zionist organizations is the pool's own and is carried into the campa rather than left in the metadata.
stops.campa: Eleven days after recognition he comes back to Washington, this time through the front door and in front of photographers, as the head of a state eleven days old and at war on four fronts. He brings Truman a Torah scroll. The recognition itself had been argued inside the White House by Clark Clifford against the whole weight of the State Department, and pressed from outside by American Zionist organizations in numbers Weizmann never commanded. He is the face that gets put on the transaction. Truman keeps the scroll.

stops.name: Rehovot, first President of Israel
stops.date_confidence: attested. Two dates were collapsed in the pool and are separated here: Wikipedia, 'President of Israel' gives the first presidential election as 16 February 1949, and the swearing-in followed on 17 February. The ceremony itself was in Jerusalem before the Constituent Assembly; the pool supplies no coordinate for that chamber and the one Jerusalem chamber pin it did supply belongs to a body that met in Tel Aviv, so rather than invent one the stop sits at the Weizmann House, which was the official presidential residence from 1949 until his death. House coordinate corrected to 31.9065, 34.8186 per Wikipedia, 'Weizmann House'.
stops.campa: The Constituent Assembly elects him President of Israel on the sixteenth of February and swears him in the next day in Jerusalem. The office is entirely ceremonial and he knows that before he takes it. His seat becomes the Mendelsohn house at Rehovot, official presidential residence for the rest of his life, standing in the grounds of the institute that the Sieff family agree that same year to rename for him. He is seventy-four and nearly blind, and he receives ambassadors a short walk from a laboratory. The renaming is dated the second of November 1949.
suggested_refs: The renaming of the Daniel Sieff Research Institute as the Weizmann Institute of Science, 2 November 1949

stops.name: Jerusalem, the Knesset returns him
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1951 (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'); day defaulted to 01. The coordinate is the pool's synthesis for the Knesset's Jerusalem seat at the time and was not independently reverified in the verification pass.
stops.campa: The Knesset returns him for a second term in November 1951. He is seventy-six, his sight is nearly gone, his heart is failing, and he is driven up from Rehovot for the occasions the office requires him at. The state he is head of is three years old and absorbing immigrants faster than it can house them. He is not consulted about policy and does not pretend that he is. He is the last man alive who sat in the rooms where the Balfour Declaration was drafted.

stops.name: Rehovot, the garden
stops.date_confidence: the death on 9 November 1952 at Rehovot, aged 77, is attested (Wikipedia, 'Chaim Weizmann'), as is the burial in the garden of the house (Wikipedia, 'Weizmann House': the gardens on the grounds are the resting place of Chaim and Vera Weizmann). Two details are weaker and are handled differently: the two heart attacks come from the pool's chronology and are kept, while its '5:55 a.m.' appears in no source the verification pass fetched and is dropped. The burial date of 11 November is [R] and unsourced in the pool. Coordinate corrected from 31.907, 34.8107, the campus centroid, to the house itself.
stops.campa: He has two heart attacks in the night and dies in the house at Rehovot, eighteen days short of seventy-eight years after his birth in a timber merchant's house on the Pina. He lies in state, and is buried in the garden of his own house as his will required, inside the grounds of the institute that carries his name, with the state and the army and the foreign delegations standing on the grass. Ben-Gurion then has the presidency offered to Albert Einstein, who declines it by letter from Mercer Street, Princeton, nine days after the funeral.
